title: Approved database interface only; no dynamically constructed SQL
objective: Make string-constructed SQL unavailable to application code and detect any database access path that bypasses the approved typed, parameterized interface, including infrastructure code, migrations and database functions.
implementing_systems: Strata (schema governance only; runtime query interface not found)
residual_risks: Strata as verified provides declarative schema management, not a runtime query interface, so the enforcing component does not yet exist.
Database functions using dynamic EXECUTE, migrations and administrative scripts can reintroduce injection outside the application interface.
Second-order injection through stored values consumed by reporting or export tools.

title: Release gate on database bypass findings
objective: Block merge and release when the dynamic-SQL or bypass scan reports a finding or cannot run, unless a time-limited approved exception exists.
implementing_systems: Praxis CI workflow (exists for tool repositories; not configured for a product)

title: No dynamic evaluation, code loading or shell construction
objective: Remove interpreter, reflection-emit, dynamic assembly loading, template evaluation of untrusted input and shell invocation from application code; route unavoidable process execution through fixed argument vectors in reviewed infrastructure.
residual_risks: Build scripts, CI workflows and developer tooling are outside application scope and still execute shells.
Third-party libraries may evaluate expressions internally.

title: No user HTML, contextual encoding and no unsafe sinks
objective: Accept only plain text or validated structured input, render through components that encode by context, and prohibit unsafe rendering sinks in source and generated bundles.
implementing_systems: Limen (exists; kernel binds data through declared attributes)
residual_risks: The Standard itself states that refusing HTML input alone does not eliminate XSS; URL, attribute and DOM contexts remain.
Limen's browser kernel is TypeScript, so script exists inside the boundary and must itself be free of unsafe sinks.
Folio-generated HTML documents and email templates are separate rendering paths.

title: Restrictive Content Security Policy and script inventory
objective: Deploy a nonce- or hash-based CSP without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval (WebAssembly evaluation permitted only as narrowly as the runtime needs), frame-ancestors restrictions and an inventory of every third-party script.
residual_risks: Blazor or .NET WebAssembly runtimes may require wasm-unsafe-eval; the exact directive set is not yet tested.

title: Cross-site request forgery and cross-origin protection
objective: Require anti-forgery tokens or equivalent origin verification on every state-changing browser request, SameSite cookies, a restrictive CORS allowlist and framing denial.

title: Server-side request destination control
objective: Allow server-initiated outbound requests only to an approved destination list enforced at the network egress layer and in the HTTP client, blocking private, link-local and metadata ranges and re-validating after redirects.
implementing_systems: Unbound outbound HTTP client wrapper (not built)
notes: Fix pass 2026-11-25 (fix-pass-agent): Outbound destination control does not cover the document renderer by itself; HTML-to-PDF rendering needs the isolated renderer in ECTL-APP-017 (OBJ-PENTEST-016).

title: Schema-bound deserialization with limits
objective: Deserialize external data only into explicit schemas and validated domain types, with size, depth and count limits, no type-name-driven polymorphism and no BinaryFormatter-family serializers.

title: Isolated file intake pipeline
objective: Accept uploads only for declared document types, verify content signatures and size, store outside any served path under generated names, scan for malware before release to users or agents, and neutralize formula content in exports.

title: Explicit state machines and server-side recomputation
objective: Represent workflow states explicitly, permit only legal transitions inside the command transaction, recompute every authorization, fee, eligibility and amount on the server, and bind updates to explicit allowed fields.
implementing_systems: Ordo state-directed engineering method (exists as a method)
residual_risks: Business rules can be legal state transitions that are still wrong; types do not prove the policy is correct.
Concurrency anomalies under PostgreSQL isolation levels require targeted tests.

title: Property-based and adversarial testing of financial invariants
objective: Exercise invariants (balanced journals, idempotent disbursement, separation of duties, legal transitions) with generated and adversarial sequences including concurrency and replay.

title: Server-controlled session lifecycle
objective: Issue sessions server-side with rotation at authentication and privilege change, idle and absolute timeouts, immediate revocation on logout or administrative action, and no long-lived bearer tokens in script-readable storage.

title: Fail-closed error handling with redacted responses
objective: Map every failure to an explicit result with a stable error code, return no internal detail to callers, redact secrets and restricted data before logging, and deny on unknown states.
implementing_systems: Aegis (exists; .NET fault capture, recovery and redaction library)

framework_refs.locator: 5.0 V16 Security Logging and Error Handling

title: Bounded input and resource consumption
objective: Enforce limits on request size, collection length, nesting depth, string length, regular expression execution time and page size at every trust boundary.

title: Release-level ASVS verification matrix
objective: Verify each release against a declared ASVS level, recording method, result and independence for each requirement so structural, automated and external evidence are not conflated.
implementing_systems: Tutela (exists; security evidence and release posture discipline)

title: Independent application penetration testing
objective: Commission independent testing of the production-equivalent application before launch and at least annually or on major change, supplying threat models without restricting tester discovery.

title: Isolated server-side document rendering (Folio HTML-to-PDF)
objective: Prevent server-side request forgery, local file read and renderer script execution when statements, receipts or grant letters are rendered from HTML to PDF with a headless browser or similar engine: the renderer runs in an isolated sandbox with no network egress, no file or other non-data URL schemes, JavaScript disabled, all assets inlined from an allowlist, and size, page and time limits; rendering inputs are generated from typed data, never from user-supplied HTML.
implementing_systems: Folio (document generation; HTML-to-PDF path outside core)
residual_risks: Renderer engine vulnerabilities (for example in a bundled Chromium) still allow sandbox escape attempts; patch cadence of the engine matters.
Fonts and images fetched at render time reintroduce egress unless inlined.
notes: Fix pass 2026-11-25 (fix-pass-agent): created for BL-016. HTML-to-PDF rendering was previously treated only as an XSS exclusion (OBJ-PENTEST-016).
